top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a mature, experimentally verified achievement with a well-defined originating idea (magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms) and a demonstrated, independently reproduced 10^-18 accuracy. The Katori and Ye allocation is stable and every committee member supports it. My own first preference, circuit QED, is not on the slate, so I judge the proposal on its merits and find it clearly worthy of an award in 2026. The citation should be kept to the lattice-clock concept and its performance, to avoid overlapping the 2005 frequency-comb prize or the thorium nuclear clock. No award is a distant second.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no documented connection to Katori, Ye or the optical-clock field
